staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the AddressSanitizer crash against this preserved vulnerable checkout. The saved line map matches `HTMLparser.c:2761` in `htmlParseHTMLAttribute()` and the staged patch inserts the missing EOF guard immediately after `CUR_CHAR(l)` in the same function.

classification.classification_note: The saved crash is an AddressSanitizer global-buffer-overflow READ at `HTMLparser.c:2761`. On the reproduced pull-parser witness, the first 8 testcase bytes make the fuzzer harness set `maxAlloc = 16`, so the second attribute-value iteration reaches `htmlCurrentChar()`'s invalid-UTF-8 recovery on attacker byte `0xFF` under malloc-failure injection. That recovery calls `xmlSwitchEncoding(ctxt, XML_CHAR_ENCODING_8859_1)`, whose HTML input-conversion path allocates a fresh converted buffer and can return an error on this witness; `xmlSwitchEncoding()` then calls `xmlStopParser()`, and `xmlHaltParser()` resets `ctxt->input->cur/base/end` to `BAD_CAST ""`. Vulnerable `htmlParseHTMLAttribute()` omits the later patch's post-`CUR_CHAR(l)` EOF guard, still executes `NEXTL(l)` with `l == 1`, advances the empty-string cursor to `"" + 1`, and the next loop-header `CUR` read becomes the ASan sink.

bug_description.original: A use-of-uninitialized-value in htmlParseHTMLAttribute (HTMLparser.c) can cause an out-of-bounds read / global-buffer-overflow while parsing HTML attribute values. The parser may read past a local buffer into adjacent global memory, leading to crashes, incorrect behavior, or potential information disclosure.
bug_description.normalized: The staged OSS-Fuzz testcase is 16 bytes long. The harness consumes the first 8 bytes as `opts` and `maxAlloc`; for this exact witness, `maxAlloc = 0x68746930 % 17 = 16`, so the pull parser runs under malloc-failure injection. The remaining 8-byte HTML payload is exactly `<h c=a\xFF `. `htmlReadMemory()` materializes that payload into a parser context, `htmlParseContentInternal()` admits it as a start tag because it begins with `<h`, and `htmlParseAttribute()` reaches unquoted attribute parsing for `c=a\xFF `. In `htmlParseHTMLAttribute()`, the first loop iteration consumes ASCII `a` and advances to attacker byte `0xFF`. On the second iteration, `htmlCurrentChar()` takes its invalid-UTF-8 handling for that `0xFF`: it reports an encoding error and calls `xmlSwitchEncoding(ctxt, XML_CHAR_ENCODING_8859_1)`. The encoding-switch helper moves the remaining bytes into a raw buffer, allocates a fresh conversion buffer, and on this malloc-limited witness propagates an error back to `xmlSwitchEncoding()`, which calls `xmlStopParser()`. `xmlHaltParser()` then sets `ctxt->instate = XML_PARSER_EOF` and resets `ctxt->input->cur/base/end` to the global empty-string sentinel. Vulnerable `htmlParseHTMLAttribute()` does not have the later patch's `if (ctxt->instate == XML_PARSER_EOF) { xmlFree(buffer); return(NULL); }` check after `CUR_CHAR(l)`, so it still returns with `l = 1`, executes `NEXTL(l)` on the sentinel cursor, advances that cursor to `"" + 1`, and the next loop-header `CUR` dereference becomes the saved ASan read one byte past the empty string.

source.description: First project-code consumption of the attacker-controlled HTML bytes on the reproduced pull-parser path. This statement materializes the fuzzed document fragment into the libxml2 parser context that later drives start-tag and attribute parsing.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is 16 bytes: `20 20 20 20 68 74 69 30 3c 68 20 63 3d 61 ff 20`. The harness in `fuzz/html.c` consumes the first 8 bytes as `opts` and `maxAlloc`, so this call receives the exact document buffer `<h c=a\xFF ` (8 bytes) and the matching `size`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: Crash sink from the saved AddressSanitizer report. After `xmlHaltParser()` resets `ctxt->input->cur/base/end` to the empty-string sentinel and vulnerable `NEXTL(l)` still increments that sentinel cursor by one, the next re-entry to this loop header dereferences `"" + 1`, one byte past the global empty string.

root_cause.description: Root cause fixed by the patch. After `CUR_CHAR(l)` has already driven the parser into `XML_PARSER_EOF` and `xmlHaltParser()` has rebound `ctxt->input->cur/base/end` to `BAD_CAST ""`, vulnerable code lacks the inserted post-`CUR_CHAR(l)` EOF guard and still advances the cursor with `NEXTL(l)` using the returned `l == 1`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The later attribute value bytes, including the exact malformed byte `0xFF`, enter project code here when the HTML payload `<h c=a\xFF ` is wrapped in a parser context.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific parser gate. The admitted document payload begins with `<h`, so this branch recognizes the input as an HTML start tag and continues into element parsing rather than comments, PI handling, or plain character data.

fine_trace.note: Source. The pull parser materializes the exact attacker-controlled HTML fragment `<h c=a\xFF ` into the parser context used on the reproduced crash path.
The document buffer begins with `<h`, so this branch admits the sample as an HTML start tag and routes parsing into `htmlParseElementInternal()`.
After tag name `h`, start-tag parsing stays in the attribute loop because the next bytes are ` c=a\xFF `, not tag terminators and not EOF.
After parsing attacker-controlled attribute name `c` and the `=` delimiter, the parser hands the attribute value bytes `a\xFF ` to the attribute-value parser.

At the start of the attacker value, `CUR` is the unquoted byte `a` rather than `'` or `"`, so `htmlParseAttValue()` calls `htmlParseHTMLAttribute(ctxt, 0)` with the parser cursor still positioned on `a\xFF `.
The unquoted attribute-value loop starts on ASCII `a`: the current byte is nonzero and, with `stop == 0`, not yet terminated by whitespace or `>`.
First loop iteration: `CUR_CHAR(l)` reads the current attacker byte `a` with `l == 1`, so the parser treats it as a normal single-byte attribute character.
The first iteration advances the parser cursor by `l == 1`, moving from `a` to the next attacker-controlled byte `0xFF` while keeping the attribute-value loop active.
Second loop iteration: attacker byte `0xFF` fails the UTF-8 checks in `htmlCurrentChar()`, so the helper reports an invalid-encoding error on the current input bytes.

After reporting the malformed byte, `htmlCurrentChar()` enters the ISO-8859-1 recovery path because this input buffer still has no encoder; on the reproduced witness this happens under the harness's `maxAlloc = 16` malloc-failure limit.

The encoding-switch helper shrinks the already-consumed prefix out of the current input, moves the remaining bytes starting at attacker `0xFF` into `in->raw`, and allocates a fresh conversion buffer before calling `xmlCharEncInput(in, 1)`.
On the malloc-limited witness, this conversion setup returns a negative result, so `xmlSwitchInputEncodingInt()` propagates an encoding-switch failure back to `xmlSwitchEncoding()`.
The negative return from `xmlSwitchInputEncodingInt()` satisfies `xmlSwitchEncoding()`'s stop condition for conversion errors.
Once the conversion-error condition is met, `xmlSwitchEncoding()` stops the parser before control returns to `htmlCurrentChar()`.

`xmlHaltParser()` sets `ctxt->instate = XML_PARSER_EOF`, frees the input buffer, and resets `ctxt->input->cur/base/end` to `BAD_CAST ""`, so the current parser cursor now points at the global empty-string sentinel.
Even after `xmlStopParser()` has halted the parser and reset `ctxt->input->cur` to `BAD_CAST ""`, `htmlCurrentChar()` still sets `l = 1` and returns the current sentinel byte to its caller.

Root cause. `htmlCurrentChar()` still returns to its caller with `l = 1`, but vulnerable `htmlParseHTMLAttribute()` lacks the later EOF check and advances the already-reset sentinel cursor by one byte, from `BAD_CAST ""` to `BAD_CAST "" + 1`.

Sink. After step 16 returned `l == 1` on the empty-string sentinel and step 17 executed `NEXTL(l)`, the next loop-header `CUR` read dereferences `*ctxt->input->cur` at `BAD_CAST "" + 1`, producing the saved one-byte global-buffer-overflow read.

evidence_limitations: The saved AddressSanitizer report proves that the sink dereference at `HTMLparser.c:2761` reads at `BAD_CAST "" + 1`.

The staged source fully closes the state transition from malformed-byte recovery to the sink through `xmlSwitchEncoding()` stopping the parser and `xmlHaltParser()` rebinding `ctxt->input->cur/base/end` to the empty-string sentinel before vulnerable `NEXTL(l)` advances that sentinel cursor.

Stage 01 does not log which individual allocation inside the `xmlSwitchInputEncodingInt()` or `xmlCharEncInput()` setup path first fails under `maxAlloc = 16`, so the GT names the shared allocation-bearing encoding-switch failure path rather than a single malloc primitive as separately witnessed.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch is source-consistent with the reconstructed root cause because it inserts an EOF-state guard immediately after `CUR_CHAR(l)` in `htmlParseHTMLAttribute()`, but Stage 02 did not execute the fixed build and therefore does not claim dynamic confirmation.
sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, patch.diff, exact staged vulnerable source, and the saved poc

cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: partially grounded: source analysis closes the path through the malformed `0xFF` byte and the unchecked `NEXTL(l)` use, but treats the final `BAD_CAST "" + 1` read as an independently witnessed sanitizer endpoint because the exact internal cursor rebind is not uniquely identified by the staged Stage 02 artifacts

format.name: OSS-Fuzz html testcase buffer
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact staged 16-byte witness. Its first 8 bytes are consumed by the fuzz harness as `opts` and `maxAlloc`, and for this exact byte sequence the harness computes `maxAlloc = 16`; the remaining 8-byte HTML payload is exactly `<h c=a\xFF `. The source-grounded trigger semantics established here are limited to that exact unquoted attribute value plus that exact allocation limit: ASCII `a` keeps `htmlParseHTMLAttribute()` in its normal loop, the following malformed byte `0xFF` reaches the second `CUR_CHAR(l)` iteration, the invalid-UTF-8 recovery enters the allocation-bearing encoding-switch path under malloc-failure injection, and the vulnerable caller still executes `NEXTL(l)` after the parser has already been halted and reset to the empty-string sentinel.
